insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured: There shall be automatic restoration of the Sum Insured once by 100%... Such Restored Sum Insured can be utilized for all claims for subsequent hospitalisation during the policy period.
great.reference: Section II (15) Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured
great.explanation: The sum insured is automatically restored once by 100% during the policy period for subsequent hospitalizations. This gives you an extra full sum insured to use after your initial claims.

great.name: Consumables
great.quote: Coverage for Non-medical Items: If there is an admissible claim under the policy, then Items as per List I will become payable
great.reference: Section II (6) Coverage for Non-medical Items; List I (Items for which coverage is available)
great.explanation: Listed consumables and non-medical items are payable when you have an admissible hospitalization claim. This means essential items like gloves and masks are covered fully.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.reference: Section III, Exclusions, 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl 01
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a standard waiting period before PED claims are payable.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.
good.reference: Section III, Exclusions, 2. Specified disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02
good.explanation: Specific listed illnesses and procedures are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a typical waiting period for such conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03 (Not Applicable for Accidents)
good.reference: Section III, Exclusions, 3. 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03
good.explanation: Illness claims are excluded for the first 30 days, but accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard initial waiting period.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalized.
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps cover diagnostic and treatment costs leading to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post Hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 90 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital.
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 90 days after discharge are covered. This supports recovery costs after your hospital stay.

good.name: NCB
good.quote: Cumulative Bonus: In respect of a claim free year of Insurance, the insured would be entitled to benefit of bonus of 20% of the expiring Sum Insured... The maximum allowable bonus shall not exceed 100% of the sum insured... Full utilization of Sum Insured and full utilization of cumulative bonus accrued, the cumulative bonus on renewal will be “nil”
good.explanation: You earn a 20% sum insured bonus for each claim-free year up to 100%, but this bonus resets to zero if fully used in claims. This rewards claim-free years but can be lost if claims exhaust the bonus.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: Air Ambulance charges up to 10% of the Sum Insured per year is payable... Note: This benefit is available for sum insured options of Rs.10,00,000/- and above only.
good.explanation: Air ambulance costs are covered up to 10% of the sum insured annually for policies with ₹10 lakh or more. This provides emergency transport support within limits.

good.name: Bariatric Surgery
good.quote: Bariatric Surgery: Expenses incurred on hospitalization for bariatric surgical procedure... Special conditions 1. This benefit is subject to a waiting period of 24 months from the date of first commencement of this policy
good.explanation: Bariatric surgery is covered after a 24-month waiting period, subject to medical criteria and sub-limits. This allows coverage for weight-loss surgery after standard waiting.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room, Boarding, Nursing Expenses... as per the limits given below; Note: Expenses relating to Associated Medical Expenses will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent/room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section II (1) Room, Boarding... Note on proportionate deductions
bad.explanation: Room rent is limited by the policy schedule and choosing a higher room category triggers proportionate deductions on related expenses. This can increase your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatment... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below; Sum Insured (Rs.) Limit per policy period (Rs.) 5,00,000/- to 15,00,000/- 2,50,000/- Above 15,00,000/- 5,00,000/-
bad.reference: Section II (14) Coverage for Modern Treatment
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered but with sub-limits, which may leave you paying extra for expensive procedures. This restricts full coverage for advanced treatments.

bad.name: Initial Waiting Period
bad.quote: Optional Cover (Lump sum on diagnosis of Cancer)... Waiting Period: An initial waiting period of 180 days is applicable from the date of commencement of this policy.
bad.reference: Section II (29) Optional Cover (Lump sum on diagnosis of Cancer)
bad.explanation: The optional cancer lump-sum cover has a long 180-day waiting period before coverage starts. This delays benefit availability compared to standard 30 days.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: No explicit co-payment clause found in the provided extract (no statement such as 'co-payment of X% shall apply').
bad.explanation: The policy does not clearly state if any co-payment applies. You should check the policy schedule or terms to confirm if co-pay is mandatory.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless facility can be availed only in networked Hospitals. For details of Networked Hospitals, the insured may visit www.starhealth.in or contact the nearest branch or refer to the list of Networked Hospitals provided with the policy document.
unclear.reference: Section IV, Conditions, 2(B) Documents for Cashless Treatment (i)
unclear.explanation: The number of network hospitals is not specified in the document. You need to verify the current network size from the insurer’s website or branch.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
